inputs.statement: Let A be any semiring satisfying the strong rank condition (every injective A-linear map A^s→A^t between finite free modules forces s≤t). Let T be a finite indexing type, and let F_t, t∈T, be additive commutative monoids with A-module structures, each free and finitely generated over A. Then Module.finrank_A(∏_{t∈T}F_t)=Σ_{t∈T}Module.finrank_A(F_t), where finrank is the natural-number value of module rank (and agrees with finite vector-space dimension over a field).

hypothesis_checks: Q is a field and hence a semiring with the strong rank condition: injectivity carries a linearly independent family of s vectors into Q^t, forcing s≤t by finite-dimensional linear algebra.
I={0,...,λ} has the finite enumeration of size n supplied by N003 and D005.
T=Q⊗_R J has its tensor-product additive commutative group and Q-vector-space structure.
Every vector space over Q is free; concretely F001 gives a finite spanning family for T, from which deletion of dependent vectors yields a basis.
F001 proves T finite dimensional by tensoring a finite generating family of J, so it is finitely generated over Q.

argument.text: By N003, J⊆C is finitely generated and nonzero, and M_R is free of rank n with coordinate decomposition J^I. Define T=Q⊗_R J and θ(q⊗c)=qc. The fraction field of R is Q: integers lie in R and every rational is a quotient of two elements of R with nonzero denominator. To see the multiplication map is injective, write any finite tensor sum over a common nonzero denominator s∈R as (1/s)⊗c with c∈J. If θ sends it to zero then c/s=0 in C, so c=0, and the tensor is zero. This also gives the usual identification of this tensor product with the localization of J. A finite R-generating family of J yields a finite Q-spanning family of T by tensoring; consequently T is finite dimensional. This proves the localization injectivity used here without presuming that containment J⊆C implies rank one.

produces.statement: T=Q⊗_R J is a finite-dimensional Q-vector space, θ:T→C is injective with image equal to the Q-linear span of J.

argument.text: Set r=dim_Q T. Tensor the R-coordinate isomorphism in N003 with Q. The result is a Q-linear isomorphism Q⊗_R M_R≅T^I: tensor the coordinate maps in each direction, and identify Q⊗_R J^I with T^I by q⊗(c_i)_i↦(q⊗c_i)_i, whose inverse sums the tensors supported at one coordinate. Finite I makes these mutually inverse. An R-basis of M_R of n members, supplied by N003, extends to a Q-basis of Q⊗_R M_R; its coefficient maps extend and prove both spanning and independence. Its dimension is therefore n. Apply M001 to the finite product T^I over Q: F001 gives finite dimension, hence a finite basis and finite generation; Q has the strong rank condition by the usual finite independent-family bound. M001 gives dim_Q T^I=Σ_{i∈I}dim_Q T=nr, using |I|=n. Thus n=nr, so r=1 because n>0 by N003. By F001, θ identifies T with a one-dimensional rational subspace of C containing J. In particular, for any nonzero a∈J and any c∈J there is a unique q∈Q with c=qa.

produces.statement: dim_Q T=1 and θ(T) is the one-dimensional Q-linear span of J in C. For every nonzero aa∈J and every cc∈J there is a unique rational qq with cc=qq·aa, and qq≠0 when cc≠0.

argument.text: Choose 0≠a∈J and a nonempty finite generating family g of nonzero elements of J using N003. By F002, write its members as g_j=q_j a with q_j∈Q×. For each such rational q_j, removing all powers of the prime p from its nonzero integer numerator and denominator gives q_j=p^{d_j}u_j, where d_j∈Z and both u_j and u_j^(-1) lie in R: neither the remaining numerator nor denominator is divisible by p. This is just finite factorization by repeated division of nonzero integers by p, and works for positive or negative exponents and signs. The resulting finite family of integer exponents is nonempty.

produces.statement: g is a nonempty finite R-generating family of J, g_j=q_j a with a≠0 and every q_j∈Q×. Each q_j has a p-order d_j∈Z with q_j=p^{d_j}u_j for a unit u_j∈R. The finite set of these p-orders is nonempty.

binders.type: index of the finite family g

argument.text: Let d be the family of exponents from F003 and set u_j=p^(-d_j)q_j, a unit of R for each index j. Let ν=min_j d_j and define b=p^ν a. Since p is prime and a≠0, b≠0. For every generator q_j a, its ratio to b is p^{d_j-ν}u_j∈R because d_j≥ν. Thus J⊆Rb. For an index attaining the minimum, q_j a=u_j b and u_j is a unit, so b=u_j^(-1)q_j a∈J. Hence Rb⊆J and J=Rb. Finally the decomposition M_R=⊕_{i∈I}J e_i from N003 becomes M_R=⊕_{i∈I}R b e_i. These vectors span, and are R-linearly independent because b≠0 and the e_i are complex independent. They therefore form an R-basis. Export only existence of such b, discharging the private choices a,g,q and their identities.
